ai.description: *Cnemaspis maculicollis* reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brown with a distinct yellow-spotted throat and a series of dark, paired paravertebral markings. It lacks precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis maculicollis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, dark, V-shaped or chevron-like marking on the nape, which is absent in similar Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis maculicollis* inhabits moist deciduous and evergreen forests in the Western Ghats, typically found on rock surfaces and tree trunks at mid-to-high elevations.
ai.behavior: *Cnemaspis maculicollis* is a diurnal gecko that actively hunts small insects on rock surfaces and tree trunks during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis maculicollis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis maculicollis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Kerala and Tamil Nadu, typically inhabiting rocky areas at elevations between 200 and 1,200 meters.
